messages:
jamie: Heads-up — Product is greenlit to roll Enterprise SLA v1.1 next Tue 03:00–05:00 UTC. This updates the SLA floor for dedicated customers (p99 latency 220ms -> 180ms) and introduces a per-tenant routing preference that biases enterprise traffic toward reserved pools. We need eng-sre to coordinate the migration window and run a staged synthetic load test. TL;DR: routing rule change + canary traffic shift + loadtest + rollback gates.

carol: Thanks — the legal/finance signoff is done, this must land in the window. We'll start communicating to customers after the dry-run. :megaphone:

maria: Can you drop the exact routing diff and canary plan here? Need to sync on observability and SLO alert thresholds before we flip anything. Also want the runbook link.

jamie: Plan sketch: 1) Preflight checks 02:30–03:00 (KV cache warm, model variants pinned), 2) Canary 03:00–03:20 (5% enterprise traffic to reserved pool), 3) Ramp 03:20–03:50 (5% -> 50%), 4) Full shift 03:50–04:20 (50% -> 100%), 5) Observability hold + soak until 05:00, 6) Postmortem and customer comms. Rollback triggers: any sustained p99 > 250ms for 5m, error rate > 0.5% 5m, or increased tail CPU on dedicated pool. Runbook: https://intranet.redwood/sre/runbooks/enterprise-sla-rollout (please add notes)

kevin: Routing snippet for traffic proxy (example):
```
route "enterprise" {
  match: header(x-tenant-tier) == "enterprise"
  preference: [
    { pool: "reserved-enterprise-pool", weight: 0.05 },
    { pool: "shared-serving-pool", weight: 0.95 }
  ]
}
```
I'll prepare the staged config patches and a canary flag. Note: reserved pool autoscale min must be bumped +20% before 03:00.

maria: Observability checklist: - pre-deploy p99 baselines for enterprise routes - synthetic probes from 3 regions - token-level cost delta dashboard ready - set burn-rate alert for enterprise-route - trace sampling at 100% for first 20m of each ramp. I'll attach dashboards and link to runbook.

deploy-bot: Maintenance scheduled: enterprise-sla-rollout by jamie on 1719523456 (Tue 03:00–05:00 UTC). Notified groups: eng-sre, eng-runtime, product, support.

jamie: Loadtest command for teams doing local verification:
```
# run from loadtest cluster
./tools/loadtest --route enterprise --duration 15m --qps 600 --payload-size small --tag sla-v1.1-dryrun
```
We'll run a global synthetic at 03:05 and 03:30; teams can kick additional region-local tests.

kevin: Bumped reserved pool min instances and prewarmed 10% of instances. Also scheduled a short maintenance window on the autoscaler settings at 02:45 to avoid noisy scaling during the canary.

maria: Quick question — do we need a fallback policy to route enterprise requests to a slightly larger shared pool instead of full rollback? That would reduce customer impact while we diagnose.

jamie: Good call. Fallback policy: on soft trigger (p99 > 230ms or error rate >0.2% for 3m) shift to fallback config: 70% reserved, 30% shared and pause ramp. Only full rollback on hard trigger. I'll add to runbook.

slo-bot: SLO update: enterprise-route p99 target updated to 180ms (effective 1719600000). Full diff: https://intranet.redwood/slo/diffs/enterprise-sla-v1.1

carol: Support will have a canned message if we enter fallback. I'll post it to #support-templates.

maria: I'll be on-call for the window and will own observability. @kevin can you be on standby for routing flips? @jamie please confirm who will own rollback ops.

kevin: I can take routing flips and rollback PRs.

jamie: I'll own rollback ops and postmortem. Will be online from 02:00–06:00 UTC.

maria: Added dashboards and alert runbooks to the runbook page. Also added a checklist for KV cache warmup: set prefix_share=enterprise:prewarm and run `scripts/prewarm-kv --prefix enterprise:prewarm --concurrency 50`.

jamie: Final note: please keep messages short during the window and use this thread for status. Reactions to ack. :white_check_mark:

kevin: ack :thumbsup:

carol: ack :white_check_mark:

maria: ack — will post live updates in this thread during the window.

deploy-bot: Reminder 30m: enterprise-sla-rollout starts in 30 minutes.
